headline: CUET VC locked in office for 15 hours amid student protests demanding former VC's reinstatement
summary: Students at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) confined the new Vice-Chancellor and others, leading to a tense standoff and health concerns for those trapped inside.
details: Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, the new Vice-Chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), has been confined to his office for approximately 15 hours. Students initiated the blockade on Monday afternoon by locking the main gate of the administrative building, trapping the VC and others inside.

The protest demands the reinstatement of former Vice-Chancellor Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem, whose removal led to widespread student and faculty unrest. Students have been observing a 'shutdown' program since September 22, halting all academic activities for nearly three weeks.

The situation escalated when the new VC reportedly broke a lock to enter his office on Monday morning, accompanied by members of the CUET branch of Chhatra Dal. Students then issued an ultimatum for him to leave by noon, and upon his failure to do so, they locked the building again.

Alongside the Vice-Chancellor, 10 to 11 individuals, including the president of CUET Chhatra Dal Wasef Rashed and some current and former students, were also trapped. Medical personnel were called to the scene after reports of illness among those confined.

A doctor from CUET's medical center examined Engineer Shahriar, who was found to have high blood pressure (170/100 mmHg) and was advised to be sent to Chittagong Medical College Hospital. The VC confirmed that two alumni members inside were suffering from high blood pressure due to the prolonged confinement.

headline: Russia strikes 6 Ukraine energy targets despite Trump's truce claim; 25+ killed/wounded in attacks
summary: Russia's latest air attacks targeted energy infrastructure across Ukraine, leading President Zelensky to question a US-brokered energy ceasefire. The strikes also resulted in multiple casualties in Kharkiv and Ivano-Frankivsk.
details: Russia launched air attacks across Ukraine, hitting at least six energy targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed. This occurred despite US President Donald Trump's recent announcement of an energy ceasefire between the two nations.

Zelensky stated that these attacks demonstrate Moscow's unwillingness to halt strikes on critical infrastructure, identifying a gas facility and a petrol station among the drone targets. He reiterated Ukraine's willingness to observe a truce if Russia reciprocated.

Trump had announced an energy ceasefire over the weekend, a claim neither Ukraine nor Russia had confirmed. This marks the second time in weeks Trump has declared such a truce without confirmation from the warring parties.

The announcement comes as Trump faces pressure over rising energy prices ahead of US midterm elections, having blamed Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries for increasing fuel costs. He had urged Kyiv to cease these operations.

In Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second-largest city, overnight strikes killed at least three people, with further attacks on Monday morning hitting residential buildings and wounding at least 22 more. Three additional deaths were reported in Ivano-Frankivsk on Sunday.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed ongoing discussions about a potential energy ceasefire but rejected Zelensky’s proposal for a broader 60-day truce. Peskov stated Moscow does not want a ceasefire, aiming for long-term peace.
Russia's recent campaign against Ukraine’s power grid, which began two weeks ago, has caused daily power cuts in Kyiv, disrupting water and sewage systems and halting underground trains.

Ukraine’s European allies expressed skepticism about the proposed energy truce, reaffirming support for Kyiv. The EU approved a new sanctions package, adding 1,569 individuals and businesses to its banned list.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for sanctions to be maintained and potentially tightened, stating Moscow would only negotiate seriously under pressure. Trump's proposed ceasefire followed his deal to buy diesel from Russia, a move criticized by Zelensky.
